preconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(line.strip()) <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each test case integer n must satisfy 2 ≤ n ≤ 10^5.
The number of test cases T must satisfy 1 ≤ T ≤ 10.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == n for line, n in zip(stdout.splitlines(), [int(stdin.splitlines()[i+1].strip()) for i in range(int(stdin.splitlines()[0].strip()))]))
postconditions.description: Each output line must contain exactly n space-separated integers.

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= int(num) <= n for num in line.split()) for line, n in zip(stdout.splitlines(), [int(stdin.splitlines()[i+1].strip()) for i in range(int(stdin.splitlines()[0].strip()))]))
postconditions.description: Each output integer must be in the range [1, n].

postconditions.expression: all(len(set(line.split())) == n for line, n in zip(stdout.splitlines(), [int(stdin.splitlines()[i+1].strip()) for i in range(int(stdin.splitlines()[0].strip()))]))
postconditions.description: Each output line must be a permutation (all distinct integers).

postconditions.expression: all(all(int(line.split()[i-1]) != i for i in range(1, n+1)) for line, n in zip(stdout.splitlines(), [int(stdin.splitlines()[i+1].strip()) for i in range(int(stdin.splitlines()[0].strip()))]))
postconditions.description: Each output permutation must be good (no element equals its index).

postconditions.expression: all(all(int(line1.split()[i]) < int(line2.split()[i]) or int(line1.split()[i]) == int(line2.split()[i]) for i in range(n)) or any(int(line1.split()[i]) < int(line2.split()[i]) for i in range(n)) for line1, line2, n in zip(sorted_output, zip(stdout.splitlines()[1:], [int(stdin.splitlines()[i+2].strip()) for i in range(int(stdin.splitlines()[0].strip()))]), [int(stdin.splitlines()[i+1].strip()) for i in range(int(stdin.splitlines()[0].strip()))]))
postconditions.description: Each output permutation must be lexicographically smallest among all good permutations of length n. (sorted_output is the list of permutations sorted lexicographically)

Instead, the expression must ensure that the output permutation is the lexicographically smallest permutation satisfying the 'good' condition (no element equals its index).
